content.text: Selecting any export action displays a success toast for the queued export action.

expected_answer.operand: a success toast confirming the selected export action

content.text: Each of Export Current View, Export Holdings, Export Transactions, and Export Risk Report is present as an export action title.

expected_answer.operand: the export action list includes Export Current View, Export Holdings, Export Transactions, and Export Risk Report

content.text: The export popover shows exactly four export actions.
CSV, JSON, and PDF are present as export format options.

expected_answer.operand: the format options include CSV, JSON, and PDF

content.text: The format chooser shows exactly three export formats.
CSV is selected by default as the export format.
Each export action displays an icon.

expected_answer.operand: every export action includes an icon

content.text: Each export action displays a description.

expected_answer.operand: every export action includes a description

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the success feedback is a directly user-visible export outcome for the investment professional. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because this flow only queues a fake export and the source states no real export is necessary.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the available export actions define the primary choices the user can make in the popover. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source describes display and selection only.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the total number of export actions affects whether the user can discover the promised export paths. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source does not describe a protected or state-changing operation.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the available format options are directly presented to the user and constrain what can be exported from the popover. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because this is a presentation choice list only.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the total number of format options affects the completeness of the user-visible export control. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because no protected transaction or data mutation is specified.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because the default format changes the initial state the user sees and may accept without adjustment. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the default concerns UI state only.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because action icons are part of the shared visible affordance for each export choice. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source describes display chrome, not protected behavior.

[risk_factors] Applied user-reach because action descriptions are part of the user-visible guidance for each export choice. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source describes explanatory text only.

[self_critique] Did not mint an AC that forbids a real file download. The source said "No real export is necessary," which lowers the required benchmark obligation to fake success feedback but does not explicitly forbid an implementation from also producing a file.
